align/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/align/hsmm.scala:56-57, in TransitionFeatures.between:

    val ps = view.relativePosition(s)
    val pt = view.relativePosition(t)

and two of the features built from them:

    TransitionKind.Backward  -> ind(s != t && pt < ps && !view.isAncestor(t, s))
    TransitionKind.LongJump  -> math.abs(pt - ps)

relativePosition substitutes 0.0 for a ref that does not resolve in the view. So if `t` is
unresolvable, pt = 0.0 and:

  BACKWARD FIRES ON EVERY TRANSITION INTO AN UNRESOLVABLE NODE from any node past the start,
  because `0.0 < ps` is true whenever ps > 0. Not an edge case -- it is nearly every source node.
  LONGJUMP BECOMES THE DISTANCE FROM THE START OF THE STORY, a fabricated magnitude that grows with
  how far along the source we already were.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE TWO SITES bd-01M1789P5B9WVNCJFN3HXACWKN NAMED, and why it is a separate
bead rather than a third bullet: signature.scala and population.scala are REPORTING. This is
INFERENCE. TransitionFeatures.between is called from transitionRow (hsmm.scala:692), which builds
the transition distribution the aligner searches over. A fabricated Backward does not mis-describe
an alignment, IT CHANGES WHICH ALIGNMENT IS FOUND.

HONEST SEVERITY, and I checked before filing rather than after. This is LATENT, not currently
firing. SourceViewLaws (laws/Laws.scala:150-157) now asserts node-totality over exposed refs for
both InMemorySourceView and StorySourceView, so no ref reaching `between` from either
implementation is unresolvable. The exposure is that SourceView IS A PUBLIC TRAIT: any third-party
implementation that violates totality gets silently wrong inference with no error, no NaN, and no
failing test. The docstring at source.scala:295-310 already records that both current
implementations satisfy the contract BY ACCIDENT rather than by construction.

WHAT THE FIX HAS TO DECIDE, and it is a real design question, not a mechanical substitution:
Backward and LongJump need a defined value when position is unmeasurable. Abstaining -- 0.0 for
both, meaning "no directional evidence" -- is fail-closed and is my recommendation, but it is NOT
obviously right for LongJump, where 0.0 also means "adjacent". THAT IS THE SAME CONFLATION ONE
LEVEL DOWN and whoever takes this should say so explicitly rather than inherit it. Consider whether
TransitionFeatures needs an eligibility concept like the one the cost model just grew.

PREREQUISITE: 3b246ea added SourceView.measuredPosition: Option[Double]. Build on it; do not add a
second accessor.

Unassigned, and I am not taking it -- I hold the reporting half and this needs someone who has not
already decided what the answer is. Anyone claiming it: hsmm.scala was unreserved as of
2026-08-29T23:2x.
set.title: align: hsmm transition features read a fabricated 0.0 position, so Backward fires on every move into an unresolvable node
